## Install Packages

```{r setup}
# Set the CRAN mirror:
local({r <- getOption("repos")
r["CRAN"] <- "https://cran.rstudio.com/"
options(repos = r)})

# Install the packages used in this tutorial:
packages <- c("cld2", "quanteda", "seededlda", "sentimentr")

for (i in packages) {
    if(!require(i, character.only = TRUE)) {
        install.packages(i, dependencies = TRUE)
    }
}
```

## Get Data

```{r load data}
bic_yt <- read.csv("youtube_comments_bic_cristal_19177.csv")
bic_reddit <- read.csv("reddit_comments_bic_cristal_1000.csv")
sailor_yt <- read.csv("youtube_comments_sailor_pro_gear_6793.csv")
sailor_reddit <- read.csv("reddit_comments_sailor_pro_gear_1000.csv")


# reviews <- rbind(
#   data.frame(bic_yt),
#   data.frame(bic_reddit),
#   data.frame(sailor_yt),
#   data.frame(sailor_reddit)
# )
```

## Data Preparation
Reddit and YouTube comments have multiple labels. Let us preprocess the data by removing missing rows of comments, keep English comments and remove non-ASCII characters. Note: current method is not scalable at all...


```{r explore}
str(bic_reddit)
print("==========")
str(sailor_reddit)
print("==========")
str(bic_yt)
print("==========")
str(sailor_yt)
```
### Reddit
```{r preprocess}
# Remove potential missing rows of comments
bic_reddit <- bic_reddit[!is.na(bic_reddit$Comment.Body),] 

# Only keep English comments
bic_reddit$language <- cld2::detect_language(bic_reddit$Comment.Body) 
bic_reddit <- bic_reddit[ which(bic_reddit$language %in% "en"), ] # Keep English rows

# Remove non-ASCII characters
bic_reddit$Comment.Body <- gsub("[^\x01-\x7F]", "", bic_reddit$Comment.Body)
str(bic_reddit)

print("=====")

# Remove potential missing rows of comments
sailor_reddit <- sailor_reddit[!is.na(sailor_reddit$Comment.Body),] 

# Only keep English comments
sailor_reddit$language <- cld2::detect_language(sailor_reddit$Comment.Body) 
sailor_reddit <- sailor_reddit[ which(sailor_reddit$language %in% "en"), ] # Keep English rows

# Remove non-ASCII characters
sailor_reddit$Comment.Body <- gsub("[^\x01-\x7F]", "", sailor_reddit$Comment.Body)
str(sailor_reddit)

```

### Youtube
```{r}
# Remove potential missing rows of comments
bic_yt <- bic_yt[!is.na(bic_yt$text),] 

# Only keep English comments
bic_yt$language <- cld2::detect_language(bic_yt$text) 
bic_yt <- bic_yt[ which(bic_yt$language %in% "en"), ] # Keep English rows

# Remove non-ASCII characters
bic_yt$text <- gsub("[^\x01-\x7F]", "", bic_yt$text)
str(bic_yt)

print("=====")

# Remove potential missing rows of comments
sailor_yt <- sailor_yt[!is.na(sailor_yt$text),] 

# Only keep English comments
sailor_yt$language <- cld2::detect_language(sailor_yt$text) 
sailor_yt <- sailor_yt[ which(sailor_yt$language %in% "en"), ] # Keep English rows

# Remove non-ASCII characters
sailor_yt$text <- gsub("[^\x01-\x7F]", "", sailor_yt$text)
str(sailor_yt)

```

### Combine Data
Keep comment data and combine data for each pen. 
```{r}
bic_combined <- data.frame(c(bic_yt$text,bic_reddit$Comment.Body)) # Combine data
names(bic_combined)[1] <- "text"                # Give column name
bic_combined$id <- seq_len(nrow(bic_combined))  # Add id column
bic_combined <- bic_combined[c("id", "text")]   # Swap columns around
str(bic_combined)

print("=====")

sailor_combined <- data.frame(c(sailor_yt$text,sailor_reddit$Comment.Body))
names(sailor_combined)[1] <- "text"
sailor_combined$id <- seq_len(nrow(sailor_combined))
sailor_combined <- sailor_combined[c("id", "text")]
str(sailor_combined)
```

## Model Preparation
Create corpus
```{r creation of corpus}
bic_corpus <- quanteda::corpus(bic_combined, 
                           docid_field = "id",
                           text_field = "text")

sailor_corpus <- quanteda::corpus(sailor_combined, 
                           docid_field = "id",
                           text_field = "text")
summary(bic_corpus,10)
print("=====")
summary(sailor_corpus,10)

```

Get sentiment score of each comment and add as variable.
```{r sentimentr}
quanteda::docvars(bic_corpus, field = "ave_sentiment") <- sentimentr::sentiment_by(sentimentr::get_sentences(bic_corpus))$ave_sentiment

quanteda::docvars(sailor_corpus, field = "ave_sentiment") <- sentimentr::sentiment_by(sentimentr::get_sentences(sailor_corpus))$ave_sentiment

summary(bic_corpus, 10)
hist(quanteda::docvars(bic_corpus)$ave_sentiment)

summary(sailor_corpus, 10)
hist(quanteda::docvars(sailor_corpus)$ave_sentiment)
```




### Processing text in corpus

Use quanteda and tokens for further processing. Remove unnecessary symbols.

```{r feature tokenization}
bic_tokens <- quanteda::tokens(bic_corpus, 
                           what = "word", # text unit to extract
                           remove_punct = TRUE,
                           remove_symbols = TRUE,
                           remove_numbers = TRUE,
                           remove_url = TRUE,
                           remove_separators = TRUE,
                           split_hyphens = FALSE,
                           split_tags = FALSE,
                           include_docvars = TRUE,
                           padding = FALSE,
                           verbose = TRUE)

sailor_tokens <- quanteda::tokens(sailor_corpus, 
                           what = "word", # text unit to extract
                           remove_punct = TRUE,
                           remove_symbols = TRUE,
                           remove_numbers = TRUE,
                           remove_url = TRUE,
                           remove_separators = TRUE,
                           split_hyphens = FALSE,
                           split_tags = FALSE,
                           include_docvars = TRUE,
                           padding = FALSE,
                           verbose = TRUE)

```


Futher processing the data. 
```{r process}
bic_tokens <- quanteda::tokens_tolower(bic_tokens) # Convert all uppercase letter to lower 
bic_tokens <- quanteda::tokens_remove(bic_tokens, pattern = stopwords("en")) # Remove English stop words.
sailor_tokens <- quanteda::tokens_tolower(sailor_tokens)
sailor_tokens <- quanteda::tokens_remove(sailor_tokens, pattern = stopwords("en"))

bic_dfm <- quanteda::dfm(bic_tokens) # document-feature-matrix (dfm)
bic_dfm <- dfm_trim(bic_dfm, min_termfreq = 5) # Remove infrequent used words.
sailor_dfm <- quanteda::dfm(sailor_tokens) 
sailor_dfm <- dfm_trim(sailor_dfm, min_termfreq = 5) 

topfeatures(bic_dfm)
topfeatures(sailor_dfm)
print("=====")

# Check for frequent undesireable words, like HTML tags.
length_features <- data.frame(count = quanteda::topfeatures(bic_dfm, ncol(bic_dfm))) # create data frame 
length_features$length <- nchar(rownames(length_features)) # extract token length
length_features[ which(length_features$length %in% c(1, 2)), ] # filter on token length

length_features <- data.frame(count = quanteda::topfeatures(sailor_dfm, ncol(sailor_dfm))) # create data frame 
length_features$length <- nchar(rownames(length_features)) # extract token length
length_features[ which(length_features$length %in% c(1, 2)), ] # filter on token length


```
No significant frequent undesireable words. So no need to remove any.

```{r}
# Print top 10 terms in the DFM
topfeatures(bic_dfm, n = 10)

# Bar plot of top 10 term frequencies
top_terms <- topfeatures(bic_dfm, n = 10)
barplot(top_terms, col = "lightblue", main = "Top 10 Term Frequencies", las = 2)

```
```{r}
# Print top 10 terms in the DFM
topfeatures(sailor_dfm, n = 10)

# Bar plot of top 10 term frequencies
top_terms <- topfeatures(sailor_dfm, n = 10)
barplot(top_terms, col = "lightblue", main = "Top 10 Term Frequencies", las = 2)

```


## Training

Training the model to output k topics.

```{r topic model}
bic_positive <- seededlda::textmodel_lda(bic_dfm[ docvars(bic_dfm)$ave_sentiment >= 0, ], k = 2)
bic_negative <- seededlda::textmodel_lda(bic_dfm[ docvars(bic_dfm)$ave_sentiment < 0, ], k = 2)

sailor_positive <- seededlda::textmodel_lda(sailor_dfm[ docvars(sailor_dfm)$ave_sentiment >= 0, ], k = 2)
sailor_negative <- seededlda::textmodel_lda(sailor_dfm[ docvars(sailor_dfm)$ave_sentiment < 0, ], k = 2)
```

## Improve model strats
### Bic

```{r}
## Remove documents that contain less than x words
bic_tokens_cln <- bic_tokens[ quanteda::ntoken(bic_tokens) >= 4 ]

## Prepare the new dfm 
dfm <- quanteda::dfm(bic_tokens_cln)
dfm <- dfm_trim(dfm, min_termfreq = 4) #Remove infrequent words
dfm <- dfm[ -which((rowSums(dfm)) %in% 0), ] #Remove empty documents

dfm <- quanteda::dfm_replace(dfm, pattern = "pens", replacement = "pen") #Replace terms 
dfm <- quanteda::dfm_replace(dfm, pattern = "pencils", replacement = "pencil") #Replace terms 
dfm <- quanteda::dfm_remove(dfm, pattern = c("pen", "also", "can", "bic", "video", "just", "pencil", "birthday", "really")) #List delete terms

#Adjust and train models
bic_positive_new <- seededlda::textmodel_lda(dfm[ docvars(dfm)$ave_sentiment >= 0, ],
                                                   k = 6,
                                                   max_iter = 2000,
                                                   alpha = 0.5,
                                                   beta = 0.01) 

bic_negative_new <- seededlda::textmodel_lda(dfm[ docvars(dfm)$ave_sentiment < 0, ],
                                                   k = 6,
                                                   max_iter = 2000,
                                                   alpha = 0.5,
                                                   beta = 0.01)

# cbind(seededlda::terms(bic_positive_new,20), 
#       seededlda::terms(bic_negative_new,20))
seededlda::terms(bic_positive_new,20)
seededlda::terms(bic_negative_new,20)
```
### Sailor
```{r}
## Remove documents that contain less than x words
sailor_tokens_cln <- sailor_tokens[ quanteda::ntoken(sailor_tokens) >= 4 ]

## Prepare the new dfm 
dfm <- quanteda::dfm(sailor_tokens_cln)
dfm <- dfm_trim(dfm, min_termfreq = 4) #Remove infrequent words
dfm <- dfm[ -which((rowSums(dfm)) %in% 0), ] #Remove empty documents

dfm <- quanteda::dfm_replace(dfm, pattern = "pens", replacement = "pen") #Replace terms 
dfm <- quanteda::dfm_replace(dfm, pattern = "pencils", replacement = "pencil") #Replace terms 
dfm <- quanteda::dfm_remove(dfm, pattern = c("pen", "also", "can", "sailor", "video", "just", "pencil", "oh")) #List delete terms

#Adjust and train models
sailor_positive_new <- seededlda::textmodel_lda(dfm[ docvars(dfm)$ave_sentiment >= 0, ],
                                                   k = 6,
                                                   max_iter = 2000,
                                                   alpha = 0.5,
                                                   beta = 0.01) 

sailor_negative_new <- seededlda::textmodel_lda(dfm[ docvars(dfm)$ave_sentiment < 0, ],
                                                   k = 6,
                                                   max_iter = 2000,
                                                   alpha = 0.5,
                                                   beta = 0.01)

seededlda::terms(sailor_positive_new,20)
seededlda::terms(sailor_negative_new,20)
```

```{r lda-topic-correlation-heatmap-fixed, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

# Use your LDA model here (e.g., sailor_positive_new or bic_negative_new)
model <- sailor_positive_new

# Get topic-word distribution matrix
phi <- model$phi  # rows: topics, cols: words

# Custom cosine similarity function
cosine_similarity <- function(x) {
  x <- as.matrix(x)
  sim <- x %*% t(x)
  norm <- sqrt(rowSums(x^2))
  sim / outer(norm, norm)
}

# Compute topic similarity matrix
topic_similarity <- cosine_similarity(phi)

# Melt for plotting
sim_df <- melt(topic_similarity)

# Plot heatmap
ggplot(sim_df, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red",
                       na.value = "red",
                       midpoint = 0.5, limits = c(0, 1), name = "Cosine Similarity") +
  labs(title = "Topic Similarity Heatmap Sailor Positive",
       x = "Topic", y = "Topic") +
  theme_minimal()

# Optional: Average off-diagonal similarity
avg_similarity <- mean(topic_similarity[lower.tri(topic_similarity)])
cat("Average topic similarity (off-diagonal):", round(avg_similarity, 3), "\n")
```





## Analytics
Descriptives

```{r}
# Extract sentiment scores
bic_sentiment <- quanteda::docvars(bic_corpus, "ave_sentiment")
sailor_sentiment <- quanteda::docvars(sailor_corpus, "ave_sentiment")

summary(bic_sentiment)
print("=======")
summary(sailor_sentiment)
```

Combining all sentiments and label them by branded pen. 
```{r}
# Combine sentiment scores and label them
bic_sentiment <- data.frame(sentiment = quanteda::docvars(bic_corpus, "ave_sentiment"),
                            pen = "Bic")
sailor_sentiment <- data.frame(sentiment = quanteda::docvars(sailor_corpus, "ave_sentiment"),
                               pen = "Sailor")

sentiment_df <- rbind(bic_sentiment, sailor_sentiment)
```


```{r}
# Boxplot
ggplot(sentiment_df, aes(x = pen, y = sentiment, fill = pen)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Sentiment Distribution by Pen Type",
       x = "Source",
       y = "Average Sentiment Score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Density Plot
ggplot(sentiment_df, aes(x = sentiment, fill = pen, color = pen)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(title = "Density Plot of Sentiment Scores",
       x = "Average Sentiment Score",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal()
```


### T-Test
```{r sentiment-visualization, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)

# Perform two-sample t-test
t_test_result <- t.test(bic_sentiment$sentiment, sailor_sentiment$sentiment)

# Visualize Results
print(t_test_result)
```

### Regression

```{r linear-regression-sentiment-pen, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Fit linear regression
model <- lm(sentiment ~ pen, data = sentiment_df)

# Visualize Results
summary(model)

# Create plot
ggplot(sentiment_df, aes(x = pen, y = sentiment, color = pen)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.2) +  # Adds scattered points with slight horizontal spread
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 4, color = "black") +  # Group means
  stat_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, aes(group = 1), color = "red") +  # Regression line
  labs(title = "Linear Regression: Sentiment by Pen",
       x = "Pen",
       y = "Average Sentiment Score") +
  theme_minimal()
```


### Chi-square-test
```{r chi-square-test-with-plot, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Combine and label sentiment data
bic_sentiment <- data.frame(sentiment = quanteda::docvars(bic_corpus, "ave_sentiment"),
                            pen = "Bic")
sailor_sentiment <- data.frame(sentiment = quanteda::docvars(sailor_corpus, "ave_sentiment"),
                               pen = "Sailor")

sentiment_df <- bind_rows(bic_sentiment, sailor_sentiment)

# Convert to categorical: Positive / Negative
sentiment_df <- sentiment_df %>%
  mutate(polarity = ifelse(sentiment >= 0, "Positive", "Negative"))

# Chi-square test
table_data <- table(sentiment_df$pen, sentiment_df$polarity)
print(table_data)

chi_result <- chisq.test(table_data)
print(chi_result)

# Visualization: bar plot
ggplot(sentiment_df, aes(x = pen, fill = polarity)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "Proportion of Sentiment Polarity by Pen",
       x = "Pen",
       y = "Percentage of Comments",
       fill = "Sentiment") +
  theme_minimal()
```
